project.name: Project Cockpit
project.summary: A DSH plugin that gives a project a holistic visual cockpit: the architecture map, the live agent team, the shared task board, and exactly which files each agent is handed. Read-only by default, with two narrow team-board actions.

components.name: Host Half
components.summary: The cordis plugin: validates and derives the project index, serves it to the panel over an authenticated /api route, registers the project_cockpit model-facing tool, and performs the two guarded task-board actions.
components.notes: No default export: the loader's unwrapExports would drop inject and the plugin would mount without its services.

components.name: Manifest Engine
components.summary: Validates the project manifest and normalizes it, reporting every problem with a JSON pointer, and rejects dependency cycles and dangling references.
components.notes: A silently misread manifest would draw a confident, wrong architecture, so validation never stops at the first problem.

components.name: Workspace Index
components.summary: Walks the workspace within bounds, resolves every declared path as present, directory or missing, and joins files to the component that owns them and the agent that will touch them.
components.notes: Planned is never conflated with present: a declared path that is not on disk is reported as absent, not omitted.

components.name: Team Actions
components.runtime: pure, over the Agent Teams service
components.summary: The narrow write surface: create a task, apply a compare-and-set transition, send a durable message. Every action is attributed to the named session's exact live Lead agent.
components.notes: Cannot touch files, spawn members, or change policy. Those stay with the agent tools.

components.name: Cockpit Panel
components.runtime: React via the shell's platform module table
components.summary: The sidebar glyph and the full-width panel: architecture map, roster against the live team, the task board, the file-to-agent join, and the findings list.
components.notes: lib/client.js is generated from lib/client/*.js by tools/build-client.mjs.

components.name: Test Suites
components.summary: Five suites: manifest derivation against a real tree, the client bundle's contract with the shell, what the panel renders, that the host plugin mounts and its actions answer, and that the shell's own client-module scanner composes the package.
components.notes: The composition suite imports the shipped ClientModuleRegistry rather than reimplementing its rules.

components.name: Tooling
components.summary: The client bundle builder, the workspace inspector, the install synchroniser, the SDK linker (which extracts from app.asar when no checkout exists), and the asar reader.
components.notes: The package must work moved, so nothing here assumes a particular location.

tasks.subject: Confirm the cockpit renders in the live GUI
tasks.description: Restart DSH so the client module graph re-composes, open the panel from the sidebar, and check all five tabs against the real project. This is the only part of the objective not yet observed.

tasks.subject: Exercise the two team-board actions end to end
tasks.description: From the Tasks tab, add a planned task to the shared board and confirm it appears with its revision; from the Agents tab, send a member its task and confirm delivery.

agents.purpose: Builds and verifies the cockpit, and owns the install it runs from.
agents.task: Restart the harness, open the cockpit, and confirm the panel against the real project before claiming the work done.

agents.purpose: Keeps the cockpit's own map of itself true, and the package relocatable.
agents.task: When a module moves or a component lands, update cockpit.json in the same change. Run `node tools/inspect.mjs` afterwards - it prints exactly what the panel will show, and the cockpit reads this manifest when it is opened against its own folder.
agents.notes: A manifest that lags the tree is worse than none, because it reads as authoritative.

invariants.statement: Planned and present are never conflated: a declared path that is not on disk is reported as absent, not omitted.
The cockpit cannot write to the project. Its only writes are two task-board actions, each attributed to the named session's live Lead.
No project is chosen by default: the resolved directory and the rule that chose it are always shown.
